q: The Post correspondence problem (PCP) is undecidable. It asks: given pairs (aᵢ, bᵢ) of strings, does there exist a sequence i₁,…,iₖ such that aᵢ₁…aᵢₖ = bᵢ₁…bᵢₖ? PCP is used to prove undecidability of:
opts: Ambiguity of context-free grammars, non-emptiness of two-tape TM intersections
exp: PCP is used to prove undecidability of various language-theoretic problems: ambiguity of CFGs, emptiness of the intersection of two CFLs, and many tiling problems. PCP reduces from the halting problem and is a universal undecidability 'relay station'.
